'''Yuri A. Barbanel''' (also '''Yuri A. Barbanel’''', '''Yury Abramovich Barbanel''') (8 April 1935{{snd}} 2 August 2016{{citation needed|date=August 2016}}) was a distinguished [[Russians|Russian]] [[chemist]] born in 1935 in [[Leningrad]] (now [[St.&nbsp;Petersburg]]).<ref>{{Cite book | last=Bower | first=Kenneth E. | author-link=Kenneth E. Bower | title=Polymers, Phosphors, and Voltaics for Radioisotope Microbatteries | date=2002 | publisher=CRC Press | location=Boca Raton, Fla. | isbn=978-0-8493-0915-1 }}</ref>  He obtained a [[Master of Science]] in chemistry from A.&nbsp;A.&nbsp;Zhdanov Leningrad State University, now [[Saint Petersburg State University]], in 1958 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1964 and his [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] in 1991. Barbanel was a scientist in the fundamental radiochemistry branch of the [[V.&nbsp;G.&nbsp;Khlopin Radium Institute]] in St.&nbsp;Petersburg until his retirement in 2011. His research interests included [[Visible spectrum|optical spectra]] induced by [[radioluminescence]] and [[Complex (chemistry)|coordination chemistry]] of the [[actinide]]s, and [[absorption spectra]] of the actinides in [[molten salt]]s.
